source_text:
Λέγει μοι: Ἆρον ἀπὸ σεαυτοῦ τὴν διψυχίαν καὶ μὲν ὅλως διψυχήσῃς αἰτήσασθαί τι παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ, λέγων ἐν σεαυτῷ ὅτι πῶς δύναμαι αἰτήσασθαι παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ λαβεῖν, ἡμαρτηκὼς τοσαῦτα εἰς αὐτόν;
μὴ διαλογίζου ταῦτα, ἀλλ’ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας σου ἐπίστρεψον ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον καὶ αἰτοῦ παῤ αὐτοῦ ἀδιστάκτως, καὶ γνώσῃ τὴν πολλὴν εὐσπλαγχνίαν αὐτοῦ, ὅτι οὐ μή σε ἐγκαταλίπῃ, ἀλλὰ τὸ αἴτημα τῆς ψυχῆς σου πληροφορήσει.
οὐκ ἔστι γὰρ ὁ θεὸς ὡς οἱ ἄνθρωποι μνησικακοῦντες, ἀλλ’ αὐτὸς ἀμνησίκακός ἐστι καὶ σπλαγχνίζεται ἐπὶ τὴν ποίησιν αὐτοῦ.
σὺ οὖν καθάρισόν σου τὴν καρδίαν ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ματαιωμάτων τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου καὶ τῶν προειρημένων σοι ῥημάτων καὶ αἰτοῦ παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου, καὶ ἀπολήψῃ πάντα καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν αἰτημάτων σου ἀνυστέρητος ἔσῃ, ἐὰν ἀδιστάκτως αἰτήσῃς παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου.
ἐὰν δὲ διστάσῃς ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου, οὐδὲν οὐ μὴ λήψῃ τῶν αἰτημάτων σου. οἱ γὰρ διστάζοντες εἰς τὸν θεόν, οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ δίψυχοι καὶ οὐδὲν ὅλως ἐπιτυγχάνουσι τῶν αἰτημάτων αὐτῶν.
οἱ δὲ ὁλοτελεῖς ὄντες ἐν τῇ πίστει πάντα αἰτοῦνται πεποιθότες ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον καὶ λαμβάνουσιν, ὅτι ἀδιστάκτως αἰτοῦνται, μηδὲν διψυχοῦντες. πᾶς γὰρ δίψυχος ἀνήρ, ἐὰν μὴ μετανοήσῃ, δυσκόλως σωθήσεται.
καθάρισον οὖν τὴν καρδίαν σου ἀπὸ τῆς διψυχίας, ἔνδυσαι δὲ τὴν πίστιν, ὅτι ἰσχυρά ἐστι, καὶ πίστευε τῷ θεῷ, ὅτι πάντα τὰ αἰτήματά σου ἃ αἰτεῖς λήψῃ, καὶ ἐὰν αἰτησάμενός ποτε παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου αἴτημά τι βραδύτερον λαμβάνῃς, μὴ διψυχήσῃς, ὅτι ταχὺ οὐκ ἔλαβες τὸ αἴτημα τῆς ψυχῆς σου: πάντως γὰρ διὰ πειρασμόν τινα ἢ παράπτωμά τι, ὃ σὺ ἀγνοεῖς, βραδύτερον λαμβάνεις τὸ αἴτημά σου.
σὺ οὖν μὴ διαλίπῃς αἰτούμενος τὸ αἴτημα τῆς ψυχῆς σου, καὶ λήψῃ αὐτό: ἐὰν δὲ ἐκκακήσῃς καὶ διψυχήσῃς αἰτούμενος, σεαυτὸν αἰτιῶ καὶ μὴ τὸν διδόντα σοι.
βλέπε τὴν διψυχίαν ταύτην: πονηρὰ γάρ ἔστι καὶ ἀσύνετος καὶ πολλοὺς ἐκριζοῖ ἀπὸ τῆς πίστεως καί γε λίαν πιστοὺς καὶ ἰσχυρούς. καὶ γὰρ αὕτη ἡ διψυχία θυγάτηρ ἐστὶ τοῦ διαβόλου καὶ λίαν πονηρεύεται εἰς τοὺς δούλους τοῦ θεοῦ.
καταφρόνησον οὖν τῆς διψυχίας καὶ κατακυρίευσον αὐτῆς ἐν παντὶ πράγματι, ἐνδυσάμενος τὴν πίστιν τὴν ἰσχυρὰν καὶ δυνατήν: ἡ γὰρ πίστις πάντα ἐπαγγέλλεται, πάντα τελειοῖ, ἡ δὲ διψυχία μὴ καταπιστεύουσα ἑαυτῇ πάντων ἀποτυγχάνει τῶν ἔργων αὐτῇς ὧν πράσσει.
βλέπεις οὖν, φησίν, ὅτι ἡ πίστις ἄνωθέν ἐστι παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ ἔχει δύναμιν μεγάλην: ἡ δὲ διψυχία ἐπίγειον πνεῦμά ἐστι παρὰ τοῦ διαβόλου, δύναμιν μὴ ἔχουσα.
σὺ οὖν δούλευε τῇ ἐχούσῃ δύναμιν τῇ πίστει καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς διψυχίας ἀπόσχου τῆς μὴ ἐχούσης δύναμιν, καὶ ζήσῃ τῷ θεῷ, καὶ πάντες ζήσονται τῷ θεῷ οἱ ταῦτα φρονοῦντες.
thought_title: The Ninth Commandment: Cast Off Double-Mindedness and Ask in Faith
orientation: The Shepherd gives Hermas the ninth commandment: put away double-mindedness and ask God for what you need with full faith.
pass_a_gloss: He says to me: Take away from yourself double-mindedness and do not at all be double-minded to ask anything from God, saying in yourself that how can I ask from the Lord and receive, having sinned so many things against him? Do not reason these things, but from your whole heart turn to the Lord and ask from him without doubting, and you will know his great compassion, that he will never abandon you, but will fulfill the request of your soul. For God is not like humans who bear grudges, but he himself is without grudges and has compassion on his creation. You therefore cleanse your heart from all the vanities of this age and from the words spoken to you before and ask from the Lord, and you will receive all things and from all your requests you will not be lacking, if you ask without doubting from the Lord. But if you doubt in your heart, you will receive nothing at all of your requests. For those who doubt toward God, these are the double-minded and they obtain nothing at all of their requests. But those who are complete in faith ask all things having trusted in the Lord and they receive, because they ask without doubting, being double-minded in nothing. For every double-minded man, if he does not repent, will be saved with difficulty. Cleanse therefore your heart from double-mindedness, but put on faith, because it is strong, and believe God, that all your requests which you ask you will receive, and if having asked at some time from the Lord a certain request you receive it more slowly, do not be double-minded, because you did not receive quickly the request of your soul: for certainly because of some trial or some transgression, which you do not know, you receive your request more slowly. You therefore do not cease asking for the request of your soul, and you will receive it: but if you grow weary and are double-minded while asking, blame yourself and not the one who gives to you. See this double-mindedness: for it is evil and foolish and uproots many from the faith, and indeed very faithful and strong ones. For also this double-mindedness is a daughter of the devil and acts very wickedly toward the servants of God. Despise therefore double-mindedness and rule over it in every matter, having put on the faith that is strong and powerful: for faith promises all things, perfects all things, but double-mindedness, not trusting itself, fails in all the works of it which it does. You see therefore, he says, that faith is from above from the Lord and has great power: but double-mindedness is an earthly spirit from the devil, having no power. You therefore serve the one having power, faith, and from double-mindedness, the one having no power, abstain, and you will live to God, and all will live to God who think these things.

choices.why: Fixed glossary term for wavering between faith and doubt; kept as a single noun throughout.
Adverb of manner; renders the force of asking with no wavering, distinct from the noun double-mindedness.
The alpha-privative adjective contrasts with μνησικακοῦντες (bearing grudges); keeps the parallel visible.

choices.english: those who are complete in faith
choices.why: Renders the adjective as a state of being in faith, preserving the contrast with the double-minded.
The verb is a strong imperative of dominion; 'rule over' keeps the command's force.
Dative of reference; the phrase recurs throughout the commandments and is rendered consistently.

pass_b_english: The Shepherd said to me, “Rid yourself of double-mindedness. Do not be double-minded at all about asking God for anything, saying to yourself, ‘How can I ask anything of the Lord and receive it, when I have sinned so greatly against him?’ Do not reason this way. Turn to the Lord with your whole heart and ask of him without doubting, and you will know his great compassion: he will never abandon you, but will fulfill the request of your soul.

“For God is not like human beings, who hold grudges. He holds no grudge, and he has compassion on what he has made. So cleanse your heart of all the empty things of this age, and of the words I spoke of just now, and ask of the Lord. You will receive everything, and you will lack nothing that you ask for, if you ask of the Lord without doubting.

“But if you doubt in your heart, you will receive none of your requests. For those who doubt God are the double-minded, and they obtain none of their requests at all. But those who are whole in the faith ask for everything, trusting in the Lord, and they receive, because they ask without doubting and are not double-minded in anything. For every double-minded man, unless he repents, will be saved only with difficulty.

“So cleanse your heart of double-mindedness and put on faith, because faith is strong. Believe God, that you will receive all the requests you make. And if ever you ask the Lord for something and are slow to receive it, do not be double-minded because you did not quickly receive the request of your soul. For surely it is because of some trial, or some transgression you do not know of, that you are slow to receive your request.

“So do not stop making the request of your soul, and you will receive it. But if you grow weary and become double-minded as you ask, blame yourself, and not the one who gives to you. Watch out for this double-mindedness. It is wicked and without understanding, and it uproots many from the faith, even those who are very faithful and strong. For this double-mindedness is a daughter of the devil, and it does great wickedness to the servants of God.

“So despise double-mindedness and master it in everything. Put on the faith that is strong and powerful. For faith promises all things and brings all things to completion. But double-mindedness has no confidence in itself, and it fails in every work it undertakes. You see, then,” he said, “that faith is from above, from the Lord, and has great power. But double-mindedness is an earthly spirit from the devil, and it has no power. So serve faith, which has power, and keep away from double-mindedness, which has none, and you will live to God. And all who are of this mind will live to God.”
